Proposed answer: Irish Parliamentary Party

The Irish Parliamentary Party (IPP) was indeed the primary political party that campaigned for the Irish Home Rule Movement. They were formed in 1874 by Isaac Butt, replacing the Home Rule League, as the official parliamentary party for Irish nationalist Members of Parliament (MPs) elected to the House of Commons at Westminster within the United Kingdom of Great Britain and Ireland up until 1918. Their central objectives were legislative independence for Ireland and land reform, and they played a crucial role in laying the groundwork for Irish self-government through three Irish Home Rule bills.

Final answer: Irish Parliamentary Party
